images.name: Neglected Flocks
images.scene: A wind-scoured hillside sheepfold has colonised the roofless service yards of a once extensive wool estate. In the upper middle, a back-facing hooded shepherd kneels to shear one thin, calm sheep with hand shears; another worker, also entirely back-facing, gathers the small ragged fleece. Make the sheep and shears anatomically and mechanically believable. Their gestures form one compact triangular group, not a row of standing actors. A low breached wall reveals the estate's mostly empty pens receding down a steep valley; one broken gate and nettles show neglect, not decorative debris everywhere. Strong oblique viewpoint from an adjoining terrace. The lower half is a coherent sweep of quiet grey-olive grazing terraces and long stone enclosure walls descending towards a distant inhabited town, with soft mist separating the planes. A pale patch of fleece in a cool overcast shaft is the single light focal point. Small wheat-coloured cloth against charcoal and muted olive; show a once productive landscape now supporting only a few animals.

images.name: Salt Monopoly
images.scene: A medieval coastal saltworks at low tide, seen obliquely across its shallow evaporation pans towards a heavy storehouse gate. Upper-centre narrative: a stooped back-facing worker offers a small basket of bread through the open part of an iron barrier; a hooded overseer behind it takes the food while releasing only a miserly wooden scoop of white salt into the worker's other outstretched hand. The two hands, basket and scoop form one decisive exchange; unequal postures and the barrier explain the monopoly without readable faces. The enormous locked salt store behind the overseer is largely full, while several production pans farther away lie weed-choked. Make these few clear narrative props human sized, not monumental. Low diagonal pan walls lead through a calm pale salt-water foreground, with an estuary and small distant warehouses establishing an entire coastal place. One dark storehouse mass balances the pale pans; cool grey-green water and wheat stone, tiny copper coin/food warmth, not an all-brown wash. Lower half has broad connected water planes and crusted pan edges with restrained contrast, not stairs or a blank plaza.

images.name: Rotting Pulp Vat
images.scene: Deep inside a once large river-powered paper mill, a roof breach has let rain rot the apparatus. In the upper centre, two small anonymous workers in patched charcoal and muted olive clothing stand beside a long stone vat: one, seen fully from behind, lifts a normal arm-span papermaking screen carrying a single torn thin sheet, while the second steadies the sagging screen frame. The small pale sheet and dripping edge are the focal action, not a giant hanging cloth. Behind, inactive drying racks and a broken waterwheel are integrated into the mill's receding structure; a glimpse through a side opening shows the stream that once drove it. Use a high oblique view along the vat rather than a symmetrical stage. The lower half continues the broad stone-sided vat and its quiet olive-grey pulp water past damp timber beams; a few broad mats of spoiled pulp reveal wasted timber without tiny clutter. Cold silver daylight strikes only the salvageable sheet and hands; warm stone and umber wood remain visibly different materials. Give roof, mill mechanism, workers and receding river convincing scale and spatial depth.

images.name: Falsified Ledgers
images.scene: An immense neglected civic counting hall in winter. Seen from the far end of a long low archive bank, a small hooded clerk and a cloaked petitioner occupy a desk in the upper centre beneath a tall cold window. Both are entirely back-facing or their heads hidden by solid hoods. One decisive corrupt transaction: the petitioner passes a few coins under the raised desk edge into the clerk's open hand while the clerk's other hand peels a blank leaf out of a ledger towards a dark document box. No writing, pseudo-letters or readable symbols anywhere. Show the physical hands, leaf and coins clearly grouped at the brightest area so corruption is readable through gesture. Neglected ledgers lie swollen and bound in orderly but sagging archive compartments; a roof stain and a collapsed distant shelf reveal institutional failure rather than arbitrary rubble. One great charcoal vault mass balances the small parchment light. The lower half is a quiet diagonal sequence of closed clothbound archive chests and a broad worn stone aisle receding through the hall, not a large empty staircase. Common palette: cool grey window light, parchment wheat, umber wood, muted olive cloth and dark charcoal, not a blue Scholar palette or uniform sepia.

images.name: Rusted Armoury
images.scene: A great stone arsenal has flooded after generations of failed maintenance. Looking obliquely across calm shallow water, see two small workers on the one surviving raised forge platform in the upper centre. Both are seen from behind with closed protective hoods or completely closed helmets, patched olive work coats, no visible faces. One lifts a modest hammer to knock thick rust from a normal-sized salvaged blade held in a vice by the other; only a narrow recovered steel edge catches the light. A very small brazier barely keeps heat, while corroded armour racks retreat into a much larger damp hall and a breached roof exposes distant battlements. The narrative is costly salvage from a ruined stockpile, not an efficient glowing new smithy. Use the diagonal hammer gesture against a great calm arch mass; humans occupy a small believable part of the architecture. In the lower half, visible shallow grey-olive water reflects broken pillars and the quiet underside of the raised work platform; a few submerged armour plates are broad integrated shapes. Warm stone and umber rust against charcoal, pale steel and subdued olive water, with one small ember accent. Atmospheric separation and sculptural material rendering, not a flat brown game sprite.

images.name: Withheld Spoils
images.scene: After a successful defense, a weary helmeted guard receives almost nothing at a fortified harbour pay station. In the upper centre, an anonymous quartermaster behind a narrow iron wicket drops a single coin into the outstretched open hand of a stooped back-facing defender; a second exhausted defender stands just behind with a lowered shield. Every helmet is completely closed and every other head is turned away under a hood. The decisive action is the tiny payment across the barrier, with clear contrasting postures: upright protected official and leaning tired soldiers. Behind the official, a heavy locked chest and two captured sacks disappear into a deep storeroom, making the unequal distribution spatially clear. Keep coins, hands, shields, sacks and people at believable sizes. View the group obliquely against one massive gate pier, with a distant damaged harbour wall and boats giving the defense a real place. Lower half shows a broad quiet stone quay curving down to still grey-green harbour water, layered towards the distant town, not a repeated empty staircase. Charcoal iron, wheat stone, umber leather, muted olive cloth; a small dull gold payment is the focal light. No readable emblems, cult marks, text or facial features.

images.name: Silted Channels
images.scene: An immense inherited irrigation system has almost ceased to work. View obliquely from a high side ledge across a ruined stone headworks and down into a whole valley of dry terraces. In the upper central 45%, three small back-facing workers use a timber lever and a fresh wooden brace to lift one crooked sluice a hand's breadth; a narrow thread of water is the only result. The gate is a real timber hydraulic gate, not an ornamental door. Behind it stagnant water is choked with reeds and silt, and a missing span of the distant aqueduct explains the scale of neglect. One worker leans with bodily weight against the lever while a second braces the hinge and the third holds the repair timber; convincing coordinated labour, human figures small beside the masonry, all faces wholly hidden. The narrow water thread leads the eye diagonally through the lower half into the dry terraced valley, broad quiet stone, soil and muted olive planes that establish a lived landscape, not a large empty canal floor. Cool grey spring air, wheat stone highlights, charcoal shadows, umber timber and muted olive reeds, with only a small pale blue-grey water accent. The material, hydraulic action and difference between former scale and present trickle must read together.
